articles.title: Formula 1 announces return to Africa with Grand Prix in Rwanda in early 2030s
articles.summary: Formula 1 will return to Africa with a grand prix in Rwanda starting early next decade once a new track has been built southeast of the capital, F1 and the country’s president said Tuesday.
articles.body: Formula 1 will return to Africa with a grand prix in Rwanda starting early next decade once a new track has been built southeast of the capital, F1 and the country’s president said Tuesday. The announcement of a 10-year-deal to hold an African Grand Prix in Rwanda comes after a campaign by President Paul Kagame to bring F1 to the continent for the first time since 1993. “This partnership is long overdue,” Kagame said at a launch event in Kigali, Rwanda’s capital. “But it is a success and a milestone for the entire continent, especially for the African fans. Ultimately, what we want is for the African Grand Prix to pave the way for other races to be hosted on the continent.” Racing in Africa will fulfil a long-held ambition for seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, the only Black driver in F1. The 41-year-old British driver has said he has been “fighting in the background” for years to have a race in Africa. Exactly when the first race will be held in Rwanda remains unclear. F1 said a purpose-built circuit was expected to be completed “early in the next decade” in Bugesera, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Kigali. The track will be built near an under-construction airport serving the capital and will “work in harmony with the natural landscape,” using hills and dips in the landscape to challenge drivers, F1 said. “Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1,” F1 President and chief executive Stefano Domenicali said. “With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.” The last time F1 raced in Africa was the South African Grand Prix in 1993. Rwanda aims for challenging circuit and economic gains Rwanda becomes the first confirmed new host nation for F1 since Qatar and Saudi Arabia joined the schedule in 2021. With a GDP per capita of just over $1,100, Rwanda will stand out on a race calendar that features glitzy destinations like Las Vegas, Miami, Monaco and Abu Dhabi. Kagame said the country aims to use the race to develop sports infrastructure and tourism and to diversify revenue. Under Kagame, Rwanda has sponsored major European soccer teams and developed a basketball partnership with the NBA, as well as hosting the world cycling championships. It’s all aimed at promoting a positive image of a country still often known internationally because of the 1994 genocide. Hosting F1 would take that strategy to a new level. “Look, our country will be watched on the global stage. And this comes with investments and creations of jobs, especially for the youth,” Betty Mukamurenzi, a university IT student in Kigali, told The Associated Press. Businessman James Ruzindana said that “for businesses, it is a challenge for us to up our game in terms of having the right products that can be consumed by those who are visiting.” The F1 spotlight could also bring renewed scrutiny of Rwanda’s human rights record and accusations of “sportswashing.” Human rights groups have accused Kagame of repressive methods keep his grip on power. The U.N. has accused Rwanda of backing rebels in neighboring Congo, and Congolese officials have condemned its soccer sponsorships. Rwanda set to outpace South Africa There have been rival projects to bring F1 back to Africa, with plans in recent years regarding three different potential venues in South Africa and one in Morocco. South Africa Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie issued a statement last week congratulating Rwanda, even before the decision was official, but still insisted his country “will get F1,” too. “We are happy for Rwanda’s 2030 F1. They have worked on it longer than SA and deserve it,” McKenzie wrote on X. “Remember though that one country, Italy, has had two F1s a year, and some react like a continent of 55 countries can only get one. SA will get F1, even before 2030.” There was no mention of South Africa in F1’s statement on Tuesday. F1 racing in Africa was linked to apartheid Many of F1’s previous races in Africa were overshadowed by the policy of apartheid in South Africa. F1 and its teams faced increasing criticism through the 1970s and 1980s, culminating in some teams boycotting the 1985 race in South Africa, which was facing various international sanctions and boycott campaigns at the time. As South Africa began to dismantle the system of racial segregation and oppression, F1 returned for two more races at the Kyalami circuit in 1992 and 1993, the last of those less than a year before the country’s first democratic elections where millions of Black South Africans were able to vote. F1 also held a Moroccan Grand Prix in 1958, the only time Morocco was part of the world championship. A project was announced last year to build a track to bring F1 back to the North African nation but there have been few updates since.

images.caption: Mohammed ben Sulayem, FIA President, Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda and Stefano Domenicali, CEO of the Formula One Group talk on stage with Naomi Schiff after announcing a Formula 1 race to be hosted in Rwanda from the 2030s during a Formula 1 announcement at BK Arena on Oct. 13, 2026 in Kigali, Rwanda.

articles.title: Billy Loughnane: Flat racing's 'Billy the Kid' set to be champion jockey at 20
articles.summary: BBC Sport speaks to Billy Loughnane, the prodigy nicknamed 'Billy the Kid' who is set to be named champion jockey on Saturday and targeting a record.
articles.body:
Billy Loughnane had never ridden in a professional race this time four years ago.

Now he is set to be crowned Flat racing's champion jockey.

And, at just 20, he's the youngest person to do so in more than a century - which means he hasn't yet shaken off the nickname "Billy the Kid".

"It's been an extraordinary couple of years, really," said Loughnane.

"I didn't think it would snowball into what it's become."

In January 2023, BBC Sport went to visit Loughnane at his family's racing yard in Worcestershire.

As a 16-year-old, he was taking the racing world by storm , racking up more than 20 winners in the first few weeks of the year - temporarily putting him top of the flat jockey standings.

He insisted then that people needed to "calm down".

While being champion apprentice was his goal, becoming the champion jockey was a dream that felt a "long way off".

This Saturday, on Champions Day at Ascot, Loughnane will lift the trophy.

When asked what he would have thought if someone had told him that when he drove up to Newcastle for his first race as an apprentice jockey in October 2022, he said: "I'd have said, 'that's absolutely crazy, what have you been drinking?'"

Despite being in a strong position to take the title, Loughnane admitted he felt the pressure "not to let it slip" until a few weeks ago.

But his nearest challenger Oisin Murphy waved the white flag, knowing he couldn't catch him, and that's when he started to enjoy it.

The final winning margin is likely to be significant - Loughnane currently leads Murphy by 29 with 222 winners.

The young star wants to break Sir Gordon Richards' 1947 record on the Flat of 269 winners in a calendar year.

"Yeah, it's in my sights," added the Irishman, who is the son of trainer Mark Loughnane.

"I'm just going to take the rest of this month in November and then assess in December if I feel it's possible, realistically. But it is in my sights, something that I'm looking towards. I'm not blinkers on full blasting at the moment, but I'm just going to keep riding every day as much as possible and assess the situation."

He could also reach his idol Sir AP McCoy's record of 289 winners, which was set over jumps as he said: "I'll be giving it my best shot until the start of December."

Loughnane wins 2,000 Guineas on Bow Echo

Loughnane sets record with 222nd winner of 2025 on New Year's Eve

Meet the 16-year-old jockey taking Flat racing by storm

Loughnane's partnership with trainer George Boughey has been pivotal to his career, and the pair have enjoyed considerable success this year.

He rode the Boughey-trained Bow Echo to three Grade 1 victories, the highlight being the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket .

"I've been searching for that feeling again," added Loughnane.

"I mean, the reception after Goodwood [winning the Sussex Stakes, also on Bow Echo] was pretty electric as well to be fair and I'm glad that I did showcase him after the race at Goodwood because obviously it was his final run. But the best buzz of winning a race was the 2,000 [Guineas]."

While jockeys are known to keep notes, few if any are perhaps quite as meticulous as Loughnane, who has a Whatsapp group just with himself, where he compiles notes on every horse he rides.

"Maybe not sets me apart, but I do think it is an advantage to be able to help," he said. "I sit on a lot of horses in the year. I've sat on over 1,000 already this year, and it's hard to keep track of absolutely every one. I wouldn't be doing my job properly if I wasn't."

So after racing on Saturday is finished and he has the trophy, what could the celebrations look like?

It's a sign of his age - and how busy he's been focused on the championship - that he has not been involved in the planning.

"My mother's actually sorted it out, so I actually don't have a clue where I'm going," added Loughnane.

"But it's with my family, friends, girlfriend, and all the sponsors and people that have helped me, sort of since I've had ponies, the whole way up, will be there.

"So there'll be a big group of us and it's more of a celebration than anything else.

"But as to what I'm eating, I'm not actually sure."

The last 10 flat racing champion jockeys

2019 - Oisin Murphy (Republic of Ireland) 168

2020 - Oisin Murphy (Republic of Ireland) 142

2021 - Oisin Murphy (Republic of Ireland) 153

2024 - Oisin Murphy (Republic of Ireland) 163

2025 - Oisin Murphy (Republic of Ireland) 143

articles.title: Dodge Nears Blockbuster NASCAR Cup Series Return in 2027 After 14-Year Absence
articles.summary: Dodge could return to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027 after a 14-year absence. A reported partnership with Richard Childress Racing's ECR Engines could help br...
articles.body:
Fourteen years after leaving NASCAR's premier division with a championship, Dodge could be on its way back to the Cup Series. And this time, the manufacturer may have found an unexpected partner to make it happen.

Dodge is nearing an agreement to return to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, according to a Tuesday, Oct. 13, report from The Athletic . Although negotiations remain ongoing, the manufacturer is reportedly targeting next February's Daytona 500 for its comeback.

If finalized, the deal would bring a fourth manufacturer to the Cup Series grid alongside Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota for the first time since Dodge departed following the 2012 season.

But the biggest surprise might be how Dodge plans to get there.

Rather than developing an engine program entirely from scratch, Dodge is reportedly working toward an arrangement with ECR Engines, the Richard Childress Racing-owned operation that currently builds engines for Chevrolet teams.

It's an unusual partnership, particularly considering RCR's longstanding relationship with Chevrolet. But it could also be the solution that allows Dodge to return years earlier than initially expected.

Dodge's NASCAR Return Could Bring an Unexpected Richard Childress Racing Partnership

According to The Athletic, Dodge initially faced a significant obstacle in its comeback plans: finding a way to supply competitive engines for an entire Cup Series season.

Developing a new engine program typically takes years, making a 2027 return difficult to accomplish without outside help.

ECR Engines now appears positioned to provide that help.

Under the proposed arrangement, ECR would build engines for both Dodge and Chevrolet. Importantly, Richard Childress Racing would not be leaving Chevrolet, and the Dodge engines would need to have distinct technical differences rather than simply being rebadged Chevrolet powerplants.

The arrangement reportedly required cooperation from NASCAR and its three existing manufacturers.

Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota have agreed to the terms, according to the report, with the understanding that Dodge would eventually pursue a separate engine supplier.

The willingness to accommodate a new competitor speaks to the potential significance of Dodge's return.

Ford Racing global director Mark Rushbrook recently welcomed the possibility.

"It's a good thing for the sport to have more manufacturers into it," Rushbrook told The Athletic.

"We want to compete against the best manufacturers in the world and to have more of that OEM (original equipment manufacturer) rivalry on track."

Kaulig Racing Expected to Lead Dodge's NASCAR Cup Series Comeback

Dodge's return would also create a new chapter for Kaulig Racing.

The organization, already preparing to field five Ram-supported entries in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, is expected to serve as Dodge's Cup Series partner.

That connection would give Dodge an existing NASCAR operation rather than requiring the manufacturer to establish a Cup Series team from the ground up.

It also fits NASCAR's reported preference for new manufacturers to partner with current charter holders instead of expanding the number of Cup Series charters beyond 36.

There is still work to be done before Dodge can officially take its place on the grid. The Athletic reports that negotiations have not been finalized, although parent company Stellantis has begun preparing for a potential announcement.

For longtime NASCAR fans, the possibility carries considerable history.

Dodge last competed in the Cup Series in 2012, when Brad Keselowski delivered the championship for Team Penske in a Dodge Charger.

It was a remarkable way for the manufacturer to leave the sport, but few would have expected its absence to last more than a decade.

Now, Dodge could be preparing to return to the same stage where it celebrated its last championship.

And if the remaining pieces fall into place, the 2027 Daytona 500 could mark the beginning of an entirely new manufacturer battle in NASCAR .

articles.title: NASCAR’s Daniel Suárez Gets Major 2027 Career Update Before Phoenix Race
articles.summary: NASCAR driver Daniel Suárez gets a major update on his 2027 future with Spire Motorsports ahead of the Phoenix race Sunday. The post NASCAR’s Daniel Suárez G...
articles.body:
NASCAR Spire Motorsports driver Daniel Suárez stands 14th in the Chase standings, 215 points behind leader Kyle Larson, meaning he still holds some long-shot hopes of a championship.

With the Freeway Insurance 500 coming up Sunday at Phoenix Raceway in Arizona, Suárez will need a stellar run to keep those faint hopes alive. Any of the 16 Chase drivers who falls at least 229 points off the lead after Phoenix will be eliminated from contention.

But on Tuesday, Suárez got a much more positive career update from the officials at Spire.

Spire signed Suárez to a contract extension for 2027, keeping its Coca-Cola 600 winner in the No. 7 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1.

The deal ends days of speculation and secures the driver who rebounded from a 29th-place points finish in 2025 to win a crown-jewel race.

"You've been asking for this. We've signed @Daniel_SuarezG to an extension for the 2027 season," the team posted Tuesday alongside a video, on the Spire Motorsports' official social media channels .

Neither the post nor Suárez's statement included financial terms or a contract length beyond 2027.

"I'm really excited to continue with Spire Motorsports. I believe in this team and, more importantly, the people behind it," Suárez said in a prepared statement, quoted by JosephSrigley.com .

"Making the Chase was an important milestone for us, and I think it shows what we're capable of as a team," Suárez said. "There's a lot of talent and determination within this organization, and I truly believe in the direction we're heading," he added. The playoff berth, in his view, validated the progress Spire made this season.

Daniel Suárez and the Path to Spire Motorsports

Suárez was born Jan. 7, 1992, in Monterrey, Mexico, and won O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Rookie of the Year honors in 2015, according to NASCAR.com . He claimed the series championship a year later.

Before that, he climbed through the NASCAR México Series and what is now the ARCA Menards Series East, according to NASCAR.com . Joe Gibbs Racing promoted him to the Cup Series in 2017 after Carl Edwards retired. Stints at Stewart-Haas Racing and Gaunt Brothers Racing followed. Trackhouse Racing hired him for its inaugural Cup season in 2021.

Suárez became the first Mexican-born driver to win a Cup race in 2022, taking the checkered flag at Sonoma Raceway in his 195th start. That season also produced his best points finish, 10th, and he added a second victory in 2024.

He also won the 2025 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series race in Mexico City at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, then captured the Coca-Cola 600 in May for his first crown-jewel victory.

Suárez's 2025 season at Trackhouse ended 29th in points with an average finish of 20.9, according to NASCAR.com. This year's average finish of 15.2 sits more than five positions better.

Spire hired Suárez in October 2025 on a one-year deal after his five seasons at Trackhouse Racing ended. "We have a path forward for multiple years, for sure," co-owner Jeff Dickerson said, as quoted by NASCAR.com .

"Daniel knows how to do this. Daniel's won races at every level, right? Won a championship," Dickerson said at the 2025 announcement.

Suárez arrives at Phoenix this weekend with one win, three top-fives, seven top-10s and 25 top-20 finishes, Srigley reported. He trails points leader Kyle Larson by 215. That 15.2 average also tops his previous career best of 16.2, set in 2017, according to Jayski .

Suárez shares Spire's three-car Cup lineup with Carson Hocevar and Michael McDowell, the format Spire has fielded since 2024, Sturniolo reported.

NASCAR.com lists 2026 as Suárez's 10th Cup season. The extension keeps Suárez, crew chief Ryan Sparks and the No. 7 team together for another season.

articles.title: El antiguo jefe de Red Bull aclara su "sueño" de ir a Ferrari
articles.standfirst: Christian Horner explica el lío que provocaron sus declaraciones respecto a Ferrari
articles.summary: Christian Horner explica el lío que provocaron sus declaraciones respecto a Ferrari
articles.body: Mientras que Max Verstappen estaba ganando el Gran Premio de Singapur, Christian Horner vivía un plácido domingo en su casa junto a su familia y veía la carrera de la forma que menos se esperaba. El ex-jefe de equipo de Red Bull Racing, concedió una entrevista a The Guardian de la mano de Donald McRae, donde pudo abrirse y contar como ha vivido este último año y pocos meses desde su despido de Red Bull. "Fue especialmente duro y triste terminar de esa manera. Pero ahora tengo una relación bastante buena con Oliver Mintzlaff (el director general de proyectos corporativos de Red Bull). Me llamó el otro día y me dio las gracias por todo lo que había hecho por el motor", recalcaba Horner sobre su salida de Red Bull, tras más de 20 años ligado al equipo inglés y con el que consiguió innumerables logros. Horner relató de igual manera como fue el proceso que vivió las semanas posteriores a su despido, donde todo su mundo se vino abajo. Tal y como comenta, no pudo siquiera procesar ese despido injustificado, en cierto modo, debido a que tuvo que apoyar al 100% a su hija, Olivia, quien estaba pasando por un momento muy duro. Ligado además a que su despido se relacionó con las acusaciones sobre las conductas inapropiadas con una empleada de Red Bull en 2024 y lo que supuso para su matrimonio con Halliwell-Horner. Sin embargo, y a pesar de los múltiples logros de Horner al frente de Red Bull, tras la muerte de Dietrich Mateschitz en 2022, fundador de la empresa y respaldo absoluto de Horner, se abrió una lucha de poder entre Helmunt Marko y Jos Verstappen, donde Horner desencajaba y la cual le acabó desautorizando por completo, hasta su final despido, tal y como el británico relata: "Helmut podía ser muy directo y me decepcionó que se hubiera quedado como invitado en nuestra casa dos días antes (de su despido) sin dar ninguna pista de que esto iba a suceder". En unas recientes declaraciones, previas al Gran Premio de Singapur, el cuatro veces Campeón del Mundo, Max Verstappen, opinó sobre la salida de Horner de Red Bull y de como el ambiente se siente menos cargante y reina la paz en el equipo desde que el británico no está al frente. Sin embargo, Horner sigue mostrando gran admiración por quien fue su protegido, especialmente ahora que le vuelve a ver ganar con un motor completamente construido por ellos mismos y tras haber pasado numerosas dificultades a lo largo de la temporada: "Me sentí muy orgulloso al ver lo que significaba para todos y que hicieran subir al podio al representante de Powertrains. Recibí mensajes de todo el equipo y le envié un mensaje a Max después de la carrera. Se mostró muy magnánimo y fue un momento histórico ver ganar a ese motor. Eso me reafirmó en la idea de que, si se reúne a las personas adecuadas con la cultura adecuada y las herramientas necesarias, todo es posible. Sin embargo, y lo que todos tratan de descifrar, es su postura con Ferrari. Los rumores de la posible salida de Fred Vasseur de la escudería italiana, se volvieron más latentes con las declaraciones de Horner, al decir que ser parte de Ferrari sería un "Trabajo soñado" Por ende, esa bola de rumores se hizo tan grande Horner ha tenido que salir a aclarar sus palabras, las cuales afirma, se sacaron de contexto, pues se refería a otras personas y no a él mismo. "Ferrari es la marca más importante de la F1. Es la escudería con más historia. Pero he acumulado un capital fenomenal que me respalda para plantearme el próximo paso que pueda dar en este deporte. Eso implicaría una participación accionarial, y Ferrari no va a vender acciones. Así que estoy contento de mantenerme al margen del deporte y ver qué oportunidades surgen en los próximos meses o años. No es un requisito imprescindible que vuelva. Solo volvería si surgiera la oportunidad adecuada con personas afines que quieran ganar. Nunca volvería solo por el hecho de participar", aclaraba Horner.

images.caption: Christian Horner junto a Max Verstappen durante el GP de Italia 2023.

articles.title: Lily, la causante del adiós de Verstappen
articles.standfirst: La bebé de 18 meses podría poner punto y final a la carrera deportiva de su padre, Max Verstappen
articles.summary: La bebé de 18 meses podría poner punto y final a la carrera deportiva de su padre, Max Verstappen
articles.body: El 4 veces Campeón del Mundo, Max Verstappen, ha admitido que será su hija Lily quien juegue un papel fundamental en las decisiones que tome sobre la F1 de cara al futuro. El neerlandés acaba de cumplir 250 Grandes Premios en la F1 y se ha mostrado muy sincero en una entrevista concedida a De Telegraaf, con Erik van Haren, sobre su futuro en la competición Esta temporada está siendo de todo menos tranquila. El cambio de reglamento, y por consiguiente, de los monoplazas, ha distorsionado por completo la forma que tenemos de entender la F1, llevándonos a un constante estado de familiarización cada fin de semana, ante lo que nos podemos encontrar. Del mismo modo está siendo una locura para los pilotos, quienes además sufren de forma directa las consecuencias de tales novedades. Sin ir más lejos, el fallo del Software en Sepang fue uno de los episodios más recientes que dejó a todo el mundo anonadado y unas críticas muy fuertes por parte de los pilotos, en especial, calificándolo de inaceptable. Max Verstappen, quien ya se postulaba como un abanderado de las críticas ante este nuevo "Campeonato de pilas", como se ha llegado a describir, no deja pasar las oportunidades para hablar sobre lo que sucede en pista y mostrar su desaprobación ante la nueva situación en la que están viviendo, incluso, tras sus dos victorias recientemente conseguidas. No obstante, y a pesar de las continuas críticas y amenazas del abandono del campeonato por parte del neerlandés, en verano renovó con el equipo Red Bull por cuatro temporadas, lo cual confundió por completo a la afición. Las amenazas de una posible retirada eran demasiado fuertes cuando el tetracampeón soltó el bombazo. Ahora, el de Red Bull deja su futuro en manos de su hija, Lily. La pequeña de 18 meses, fruto de su relación con Kelly Piquet, podría ser la "culpable" de la retirada de Verstappen de la F1. "La verdad es que, ahora, después de una carrera, siempre intento volver directamente a casa el domingo por la tarde. Para pasar el mayor tiempo posible en casa", relataba el neerlandés. Y es que, en todo momento Verstappen ha mostrado la importancia que supone la pequeña Lily en su vida, así como Penelope, a pesar de no ser su hija biológica: "Cuando está durmiendo, no la despierto. Como es lógico, la dejo descansar. Pero a menudo voy a ver cómo está un momento, sin molestarla. Y en cuanto se despierta, quiero pasar todo el tiempo que pueda con ella". Es por ello que Verstappen ve una posible retirada de la F1 más pronto incluso de lo que nos podamos esperar pues, tal y como el mismo relató, la pequeña ya empieza a darse cuenta de las ausencias de su padre, algo que parece atormentar a Max: "Eso también será algo a tener en cuenta más adelante, cuando se trate de mi futuro. No quiero estar fuera todo el tiempo; quiero ver crecer a mis propios hijos. Porque, una vez que cumplan dieciocho años, es posible que me digan “adiós” y den un portazo al salir".

images.caption: Max Verstappen tras conseguir su 4º Título Mundial de F1 en 2024.

articles.title: George Russell: Mercedes driver planning to take another grid penalty for upgraded power unit element at Las Vegas Grand Prix
articles.summary: George Russell has revealed he plans to take a grid penalty at next month's Las Vegas Grand Prix to allow an upgraded power unit element to be fitted to his car; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Russell started at the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change following an engine issue at the previous race in Malaysia which saw him retire late on.

He recovered to ninth but now trails Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli by 102 points in the Drivers' Championship with six rounds remaining, so is all but mathematically out of the title fight.

Prior to his Malaysia reliability woes, Mercedes had planned for Russell to take on a new power unit at the United States Grand Prix, which takes place next weekend in Austin, as they expect to have an upgrade ready, but it appears Russell will take on the new part three races later in Las Vegas on November 20-22.

Mercedes are taking up the upgrade opportunity they were granted by the FIA's ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) system to improve their engine.

The ranking of Mercedes' engine performance below Red Bull's by the sport's governing body caused some dispute, with the Milton Keynes squad arguing that the Silver Arrows, who are dominating the Constructors' Championship, already have the best power unit.

"It will probably be later in the season now to be honest - maybe Las Vegas. But it will be there at some point," Russell told Sky Sports F1 when asked when he will take on the upgraded power unit element that will trigger a grid penalty.

"Now we have the choice to take it when we wish and we will choose slightly easier tracks [to overtake at]."

Russell: Goal is to get on top of upgrades

Russell came into 2026 as favourite for the championship with many pundits predicting Mercedes would have the best car and Antonelli, in just his second F1 season, not ready to challenge for the title. However, Russell has largely been outpaced by Antonelli with just three wins to the Italian's eight this season.

Mercedes brought an upgrade package to Malaysia which did not give them the instant performance they anticipated, so ran the pre-Malaysia car with Russell and the new upgrades with Antonelli in Singapore.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen topped every competitive session of the Sprint weekend in Singapore, although Russell was leading the Sprint race until he crashed.

"The goal right now is to try to improve the car. We were very much the dominant team for this whole season," said Russell.

"You look at the recent races and Red Bull have been very much best. In Baku, Max was a similar level to me. We go to Malaysia, a totally different track, and Singapore another different track, and he's dominated the last two weekends.

"Right now, the goal is to try and get on top of these updates."

Antonelli finished on the podium in Sunday's race after making late overtakes on McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

The championship leader finished 25 seconds behind race-winner Max Verstappen and thinks Red Bull have done an "incredible step forward", while Mercedes are yet to extract the most from their own upgrades.

"I feel like it was a very progressive weekend, where we started off the pace and I've definitely been struggling with the new package," Antonelli said.

"But the team did incredibly well on putting the car in a better window. And now we understand a lot more the aero package, how it works, which is very different compared to the old one. It's about trying to find the right window for the car.

"All in all, I feel like we're seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and we're going to keep pushing on this package because, also on my side, I want to help the team as much as possible in trying to understand it, also to understand which way to take for the future car as well."

articles.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Il Est Francais makes stable debut for Dan Skelton
articles.summary: The 2023 Kauto Star Novices' Chase winner Il Est Francais will look to discover his mojo when he makes his first start for the Skelton team at Ffos Las this afternoon; The card at the South Wales track features some other National Hunt stars, including Paul Nicholls' Tutti Quanti.
articles.body:
4.38 Ffos Las - Il Est Francais debuts for the Skelton brigade

A host of big names arrive at Ffos Las on Wednesday, with Il Est Francais a fascinating contender in this Faucets Handicap Chase .

A dual Grade 1 winner, including the Kauto Star Novices' Chase back in 2023, he has a point to prove having been pulled up on his past three starts. The move to a new yard may spark a return to form but he will need to be at the top of his game to concede weight all round.

Jonjo and AJ O'Neill's Crebilly heads a long list of alternatives. He doubled his tally over fences when scoring at Worcester on his last outing in September and will have a fitness edge over his rivals.

Saint Segal enjoyed a successful season last year, winning on two occasions. He should appreciate the drop into handicaps having contested top-level events in the spring.

Torneo , Down Memory Lane and Southoftheborder rate each-way players.

3.30 Ffos Las - Tutti Quanti and Captain Teague clash

A brilliant field has assembled for this Listed Adept GRP Cabinets Novices' Chase , where Tutti Quanti heads four runners.

The Paul Nicholls-trained six-year-old ran out a wide-margin winner of the William Hill Hurdle in February before finishing well beaten in the Champion Hurdle. This 151-rated hurdler has long been viewed as a chaser, and he could prove a class apart on his fences debut under Sam Twiston-Davies.

Captain Teague makes his debut for Dan Skelton having switched from the Paul Nicholls yard. A Grade 1 winner as a novice hurdler, he scored on his first start over fences before suffering a setback at Newbury. Having reverted to hurdles since then, it is hoped he can get back on track in this sphere.

George's Lad dominated a decent field when winning easily at Haydock in April and makes appeal on his fencing bow, while Tamarind Bay cannot be dismissed. A winner of three of his five starts over fences, his experienced could see him go close.

2.20 Ffos Las - Sinnatra and Pourquoi Pas Papa head over fences

Sinnatra and Pourquoi Pas Papa headline an excellent line-up for this JCP Solicitors Novices' Limited Handicap Chase at 2.20pm.

Dan Skelton's Sinnatra improved with each outing over hurdles, ending the campaign with a superb second behind Storming George at Aintree. He now tackles fences on this handicap debut and this imposing type could be even better in this discipline.

Pourquoi Pas Papa looks a huge threat for Paul Nicholls and Sam Twiston-Davies. Just a four-year-old, he will receive a hefty weight allowance and having placed at the Aintree festival on his last start, he rates a smart prospect.

Light Fandango seeks a third win on the bounce having won a couple of handicap hurdles at Doncaster and Musselburgh and must be feared given a clear round.

Wandering Ego and Desertmore News complete a cracking quintet.

Nocte Volatus , Ben Solo and Iron Bridge feature in the 2.55pm RWK Goodman Veterans' Handicap Chase , with the latter looking to continue where he left off after scoring at Haydock when last seen back in April.

Fresh from putting five rivals to the sword at Worcester last week, King Roly looks to go in again for Mickey Bowen in the Adept GRP Cabinets Native River Handicap Chase at 4.05pm. Here, he takes on Viroflay , who now has a mark of 144 after winning at Newton Abbot by an enormous margin last time.

The card ends with the 5.13pm Enigma Flooring Handicap Chase , with Yes Day and Jaccours the likely market principles.

articles.title: Alonso y Honda, de contradicción en contradicción
articles.standfirst: El asturiano volvió a ofrecer un diagnóstico que el motorista japonés descarta pese al pobre rendimiento del paquete completo
articles.summary: El asturiano volvió a ofrecer un diagnóstico que el motorista japonés descarta pese al pobre rendimiento del paquete completo
articles.body: El reciente Gran Premio de Singapur fue, como ya es sabido, un bajón en las expectativas de Aston Martin. En el seno de la escuadra británica se miraba con optimismo a la pista del sudeste asiático, aunque siempre con cierta cautela. "Esperábamos meter, al menos, a un coche en Q2", deslizó Mike Krack, su responsable en pista. Pero el listón de la zona competitiva se colocó en un lugar inalcanzable, y Fernando Alonso, su estrella, señaló al problema de toda la temporada: el motor. La evolucionada unidad de potencia de Honda no respondió como el piloto quería y el asturiano no se cortó en ningún momento para hacerlo ver. Como resultado, el triplete entre Bakú, Sepang y Singapur se saldó con la gran noticia del mejor resultado de la temporada, pero también con dos momentos de contradicción entre Alonso y Honda. Cuando el rendimiento no apareció, el bicampeón reportó problemas que los japoneses descartaron. "Había algo anómalo en el motor", dijo en Bakú, donde tuvo que abandonar. Pero Shintaro Orihara, responsable en pista de la firma asiática, lo descartó. "Según los datos que tenemos ahora y tras revisarlo todo, vemos el motor bien", lanzó. Cosa que se repitió 15 días después en Singapur tras otra actuación mala. En este caso, Alonso reportó problemas del motor (enfocados en el turbo) que desde el seno de Aston Martin parecían confirmarse. Pero Orihara, de nuevo, negó que estuviese roto. "No lo estaba. Lo cambiamos por las sensaciones del piloto, que son el mejor medidor", relató. Sí que Honda aceptó para cambiarlo entre sábado y domingo, pero señalan a la petición del bicampeón. Otra gran contradicción. Y que profundiza en la lista interminable de problemas de la unidad de potencia. En casi todas las circunstancias. "En este circuito hay un punto difícil en la energía, en este circuito [Singapur] cambia la potencia de recarga en cada curva", comentó el japonés. Y abre el abanico de factores a los que señalar. "No hay diferencia de rendimiento que provenga de la potencia en sí. La gestión de energía, manejabilidad y boost también influye", añadió. El cruce de discursos recuerda directamente a los de la primera etapa del asturiano al lado del motorista japonés. Pero antes de juzgar nada con rotundidad, el futuro es el que se examinará con la nueva unidad de potencia de 2027. El 2026 queda como el de tareas de aprendizaje e intentar solventar la situación lo mejor posible, y el salto tiene que llegar. Eso sí, el crédito no es infinito. "No pudo esperar otros cinco años", relató el piloto español. En el paddock todos concuerdan en que Honda llegará, pero el asturiano pone una fecha en el horizonte. Que también tiene que ver con la renovación de hace unas semanas. Alonso nunca ha renunciado a seguir peleando por grandes resultados, en Aston Martin tiene casi todo para formar un equipo único (presupuesto, instalaciones y nombres en la dirección) y la duda final es ese motor. La primera experiencia como equipo oficial de Honda no es buena, queda claro desde aquella rueda de prensa en Newey en Australia, pero mantienen la confianza para dar al piloto unas herramientas a la altura. "Llegarán, seguro", repiten en el equipo verde. Aunque la luz sigue estando alejada en el túnel. Y el 2027, con la reducción de la potencia eléctrica y aumento del poder de la combustión, ya aparece como un examen... final para el proyecto.
